title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: A code editor wants to warn about unmatched brackets. Write a function that returns true when every opening bracket is closed by the correct type of bracket in the correct order. Brackets may be (), [], or {}.

explanation.beginner:
Example: validParentheses("({[]})") produces true. Push opening delimiters onto a stack. A closing delimiter must match the most recent unmatched opener, then remove it. The stack must be empty at the end.

Compare “rejects mismatched pairs”: input ["([)]"] produces false. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Push opening delimiters onto a stack. A closing delimiter must match the most recent unmatched opener, then remove it. The stack must be empty at the end.

Tempting mistake: Equal numbers of opening and closing symbols do not prove correct nesting: ([)] has balanced counts and wrong order.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. One scan costs O(n) time and up to O(n) stack space.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “rejects mismatched pairs”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
